channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula mantém liderança no 1º turno, mas segue numericamente atrás de Flávio no 2º, mostra pesquisa AtlasIntel
item.description: Lula maintains his lead in the first round of the 2026 presidential election, according to an AtlasIntel poll released on April 28. However, in a potential second-round scenario, he trails numerically behind Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, though within the margin of error, indicating a technical tie.

item.title: Morador é abordado por faixa com “ladrão” perto de evento de Lula
item.description: A resident of Presidente Prudente (SP) was approached by men identified as Federal Police agents after displaying a banner reading 'thief' on his apartment window near an event with President Lula. The video of the encounter was shared by pre-candidates Flávio Bolsonaro and Nikolas Ferreira, who criticized the action as censorship. There is no official confirmation from the PF regarding the agents' identity or the legality of the approach.

item.title: Pesquisa expõe cansaço dos eleitores de Minas com a polarização e traz péssima notícia a Zema
item.description: The Genial Quaest poll shows that although 52% approve of Romeu Zema's management in Minas Gerais, only 13% want his continuation, with 44% demanding a complete change in administration. Voters exhibit fatigue with polarization: 37% prefer an independent governor, while Cleitinho Azevedo leads the presidential race with 30% voting intentions, ahead of Alexandre Kalil (14%) and Rodrigo Pacheco (8%).

item.title: Quaest: 52% aprovam e 41% desaprovam governo Romeu Zema em MG
item.description: The Quaest poll shows 52% of Minas Gerais voters approve of former governor Romeu Zema's (Novo) government, while 41% disapprove, with 6% undecided. Zema resigned in March to run for president in 2026, and the state is currently led by Vice Governor Mateus Simões (PSD). The survey also found that 44% of voters believe the next governor should completely change the current government, compared to only 13% who support continuity.

item.title: Partido Liberal de Bolsonaro quer tabelar preços dos combustíveis
item.description: The Liberal Party, once a defender of economic orthodoxy, now supports a proposal by Senator Marcos Rogério (PL-RO) to cap fuel prices during crises, breaking with international parity and advocating state intervention in the market. Despite historical inefficacy, this shift reflects the party’s ideological transformation under Jair Bolsonaro’s influence, who has designated his son Flávio Bolsonaro as the PL’s presidential candidate for 2026.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: governo de Minas tem piora na avaliação e queda na aprovação, enquanto Zema tenta projeção nacional
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that approval of Romeu Zema's government in Minas Gerais dropped from 62% in February 2025 to 52% in April 2026, with disapproval rising from 30% to 41%. Negative evaluation of the administration nearly doubled, from 14% to 26%, and 49% of voters believe Zema does not deserve to elect a successor, indicating strong rejection of his political group's continuity. Despite declining approval, Zema is gaining national visibility through clashes with the STF, particularly Justice Gilmar Mendes, boosting his profile as a potential presidential candidate.

item.title: Governo Zema tem aprovação de 52% dos mineiros, diz Quaest
item.description: A Quaest poll released on April 28, 2026, shows 52% of Minas Gerais voters approve of former governor Romeu Zema's (Novo) administration, while 41% disapprove. Government evaluation reveals 32% positive, 36% regular, and 26% negative ratings. Zema, re-elected in 2022, is barred from running for a third term in 2026 under Brazilian re-election laws.

item.title: Alcolumbre decide não receber Messias e influência dele deve definir destino de indicação ao STF
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) has declined to meet with STF nominee Jorge Messias to maintain neutrality, despite having previously warned the Lula government about Senate resistance. His influence over 12 to 15 undecided senators aligned with the 'centrão' bloc may determine the outcome, as favorable vote projections have dropped from 46 to 44. The government is attempting to sway votes through parliamentary amendment negotiations, but senators remain resistant, leaving the nomination in a tight spot with 25 firm supporters, 35 opponents, and 21 undecided.

item.title: PGR blinda Gilmar e arquiva pedido de investigação por homofobia
item.description: The Prosecutor General's Office archived a request to investigate Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes for alleged homophobia following an interview with Metrópoles, in which he criticized presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema of the Novo party. The request accused Mendes of making an 'injurious accusation' against Zema, but the PGR found insufficient grounds to initiate a civil public action.

item.title: Crusoé: Zema encosta em Lula no segundo turno, indica AtlasIntel
item.description: An AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll shows Romeu Zema (Novo) narrowing the gap with Lula (PT) in a hypothetical runoff, rising from 43.7% to 46.5% in voting intentions, while Lula increased slightly from 46.6% to 47.4%. The result indicates a technical tie within the margin of error, with Zema gaining ground against the president.

item.title: Desenrola 2.0: 8 perguntas e respostas sobre o programa que dará desconto em dívidas
item.description: The Lula government is preparing to launch Desenrola 2.0, a debt renegotiation program offering discounts of 20% to 90% on bank debts and interest rates below 2% per month, initially targeting individuals earning up to five minimum wages. Announced ahead of May 1st, the initiative aims to ease household financial strain and boost purchasing power in an election year, responding to rising indebtedness and delinquency, as well as Flávio Bolsonaro's growing poll numbers.

item.title: AtlasIntel: Lula lidera no 1º turno e empata tecnicamente com Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º
item.description: Lula leads in all first-round scenarios tested by AtlasIntel/Bloomberg, while Flávio Bolsonaro is technically tied with him in a potential runoff, at 47.8% to 47.5% — a mere 0.3 percentage point difference. Romeu Zema follows as the second most competitive opponent with a 0.9-point deficit, while Ronaldo Caiado and Renan Santos trail significantly. The survey interviewed 5,008 voters across Brazil’s five regions from April 22–27, with a 95% confidence level and a 1-point margin of error.

item.title: Emissário de Alcolumbre orienta senadores a votar contra Messias; presidente do Senado nega
item.description: An emissary close to Davi Alcolumbre contacted senators urging them to vote against Jorge Messias' STF nomination, two days before the CCJ hearing. The Senate president denied knowledge of the emissary's actions. The report is subscriber-only.

item.title: Lula é desaprovado por 52,5% da população e aprovado por 46,8%, diz pesquisa
item.description: The Atlas/Bloomberg poll shows President Lula with 52.5% disapproval and 46.8% approval, reflecting a slight improvement since March (approval up 0.8%, disapproval down 1.5%). He has the highest rejection rate among mentioned politicians, with 51% saying they would never vote for him, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (49.8%) and Jair Bolsonaro (44.9%).

item.title: Lula é desaprovado por 52,5% e aprovado por 46,8%, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: An AtlasIntel survey shows 52.5% of Brazilian voters disapprove of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government, while 46.8% approve, with a 1-point margin of error. Conducted April 22–27, 2026 among 5,008 respondents, the poll finds 51.3% rate the administration as 'bad' or 'terrible', compared to 42% who see it as 'excellent' or 'good'. Registered with the TSE as BR-07992/2026, the study was self-funded by AtlasIntel at a cost of R$75,000.

item.title: AtlasIntel: 51% rejeitam voto em Lula e 49,8%, em Flávio
item.description: According to an AtlasIntel poll released on April 28, 2026, 51% of respondents reject voting for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), while 49.8% reject voting for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). The survey, conducted between April 22 and 27 with 5,008 Brazilian voters, also found that 47.3% fear Lula’s re-election and 45.4% fear Flávio Bolsonaro’s election. Jair Bolsonaro registered 44.9% rejection and Renan Santos 42.2%.

item.title: Governo Lula quer suspender bancos que cobram “juro abusivo”
item.description: The Lula government aims to suspend or revoke the authorization of banks charging abusive interest rates in payroll-deductible loans under the Workers’ Credit program, using a formula based on weighted average rate, standard deviation, and an undisclosed multiplier. The Ministry of Labor and Employment refused to disclose which rates would be deemed abusive, despite requests for clarification and hypothetical examples, raising transparency concerns. Data shows some institutions charge over 100% annual interest, peaking at 123.54%, while the average stood at 56.77% in March.

item.title: TSE retoma nesta 3ª feira julgamento que pode cassar governador de RR
item.description: The TSE resumes the trial that could remove the mandate of Roraima's governor, Edilson Damião (União Brasil), after a suspension in April. Minister Nunes Marques voted to acquit Damião but upheld the ineligibility of former governor Antonio Denarium, citing lack of evidence of Damião's participation in the alleged irregularities and Denarium's resignation as a new institutional fact. Ministers Estela Aranha, Floriano de Azevedo Marques, Antonio Carlos Ferreira, and Cármen Lúcia still need to vote.

item.title: Indicação de Otto Lobo à CVM segue em banho-maria no Senado e relator quer conversa com Lula
item.description: Senator Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM), appointed as rapporteur for Otto Lobo's nomination to lead the CVM in the Senate's Economic Affairs Committee, is reviewing his report on Lula's January 6 nomination. Braga wants to speak with President Lula before finalizing his report, as Lobo's nomination is considered controversial. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: “Rejuvenescido e equilibrado”: como PT apresentará Lula na campanha. Vídeo
item.description: Lula’s 2026 re-election campaign has defined a new marketing strategy based on attributes such as 'rejuvenated', 'experienced', 'balanced', 'firm', and 'respected', according to voter research. Marketer Raul Rabelo emphasized that Lula remains healthy at 80, maintaining physical and mental strength, as a counter to opposition attacks on his age. The presentation took place at the 8th National Congress of the PT in Brasília.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonarinho: dê ouvidos ao seu irmão que ele sabe das coisas
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro, the most politically experienced son of Jair Bolsonaro, publicly warns his brother Flávio about the dangers of ignoring his political advice, recalling that he led Jair’s victorious 2018 presidential campaign. Despite Flávio being stripped of his social media access by Jair after a humiliating incident in 2016 and receiving only 14% in Rio’s mayoral race, Carlos continues to counsel him, while Flávio appears to repeat his father’s mistake by sidelining him.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro elabora defesa em nova investigação aberta por Moraes
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has outlined his defense strategy in the inquiry opened by Justice Alexandre de Moraes (STF) over alleged slander against President Lula, claiming parliamentary immunity and framing his January post about Nicolás Maduro as referring to crimes committed by the Venezuelan president. His lawyers argue the post was made in the exercise of his mandate and that the 60-day PF investigation window is favorable, delaying any potential PGR indictment and STF review.

item.title: Governadora recebe alerta: é melhor privatizar BRB do que ter liquidação e seu ‘enterro político’
item.description: The governor of the Federal District, Celina Leão, opposes the privatization of the Bank of Brasília (BRB) due to electoral concerns, despite experts warning that the bank's liquidation would be even more damaging to her re-election prospects. The BRB faces insolvency risk due to the GDF's R$ 926.5 million budget deficit in 2025 and the FGC's refusal to provide loans, increasing pressure on the Central Bank to order an extrajudicial liquidation. Meanwhile, the BRB is delaying the release of its financial statements to avoid formally confirming its dire financial situation.

item.title: Kassab diz que Lula sabe gastar, mas não sabe administrar
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD, said President Lula knows how to spend but not how to administer the public machine efficiently, despite acknowledging good social programs. He noted that Lula inherited a favorable scenario from FHC, but the PT administration lost efficiency over time. Kassab also stated he does not see Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro as winners in 2026 due to high rejection rates and endorsed Ronaldo Caiado as the PSD’s most complete candidate, with no corruption allegations in 40 years of public life.

item.title: Messias precisa de metade dos senadores que evitam declarar voto para garantir vaga no STF e mira no centro, mostra levantamento
item.description: Jorge Messias, nominee for the Supreme Federal Court (STF), has 25 favorable votes and 22 opposed in the Senate, needing 16 of the 34 undecided or non-committal senators to reach the 41 votes required for approval. The MDB and PSD, center parties supporting the Lula government, hold the largest share of this undecided bloc, with senators like Omar Aziz, Nelsinho Trad, and Marcelo Castro still without public positions. Opposition, led by the PL, is more unified against the nomination, with critics like Marcos Pontes challenging the political model of STF appointments.

item.title: PGR arquiva pedido para investigar Gilmar Mendes por homofobia
item.description: The Attorney General's Office (PGR) archived a request to investigate Gilmar Mendes for homophobia following the Supreme Court minister's comments that homosexuality could be a 'defamatory accusation' against pre-candidate Romeu Zema. The case involved references to the former Minas Gerais governor as a pre-candidate for the Novo party in the 2026 presidential election.

item.title: Os planos de Renan Santos para roubar votos de Flávio Bolsonaro: 'Sou o candidato da direita'
item.description: Renan Santos, a pre-candidate for the Presidency from the Mission party, claims he is the right-wing candidate and positions Flávio Bolsonaro as a centrist, aiming to draw right-wing voters through confrontation and attack rhetoric. He stated he wants to 'end the race of Flávio Bolsonaro' and could prevent the election from being decided in the first round, according to analysts. His strategy focuses on attacking Bolsonaro to capture votes from a young, anti-establishment electorate.

item.title: Governo Lula tenta blindar Messias em sabatina e afastar risco de rejeição
item.description: The Lula government is mobilizing efforts to shield Jorge Messias's STF nomination, aiming to avoid embarrassment during his Senate CCJ hearing and reduce the risk of rejection in a secret vote. Messias needs at least 41 votes for confirmation, and even his allies expect a tight vote on Wednesday, the 29th. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Governo estuda modelo de portabilidade de crédito para Desenrola de micro e pequenas empresas. Entenda
item.description: The Lula government is studying a credit portability model for micro and small businesses in the upcoming edition of the Desenrola program, allowing debts to be transferred to banks offering lower interest rates and reduced installments, unlike the refinancing approach for individuals. The target audience includes businesses with annual gross revenue of up to R$ 4.8 million, with a planned launch by May 1st, though the business-focused announcement may be delayed as discussions remain in early stages.

item.title: Às vésperas de sabatina de Messias, governo empenha R$ 12 bilhões em emendas em abril
item.description: The federal government committed R$12 billion in parliamentary amendments in April, on the eve of Jorge Messias’ STF confirmation hearing, representing over 58% of the mandatory first-half 2026 total. This increase coincides with political negotiations to secure the votes needed for his appointment, amid opposition from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. The largest Senate caucuses — PL, MDB, and PSD — received the highest amounts, while the PT ranked fourth.

item.title: Abono salarial: após mudanças, 4,5 milhões de trabalhadores deixarão de receber o benefício até 2030
item.description: The Ministry of Labor estimates that 4.56 million workers will stop receiving the wage bonus between 2026 and 2030 due to rule changes that will adjust the income threshold only for inflation, while the minimum wage gains real growth. In 2026, 559,000 workers will lose the benefit, rising to 1.58 million in 2027, as the eligibility cap drops to 1.89 minimum wages. The measure aims to ensure the sustainability of the Workers’ Support Fund (FAT) and long-term fiscal responsibility, targeting the benefit toward lower-income workers.

item.title: Dino deve conversar com relatores no STF antes de liberar vista de julgamento sobre eleições no Rio
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino plans to consult with rapporteurs Cristiano Zanin and Luiz Fux before releasing his view on the Rio de Janeiro interim governorship election case. He is awaiting completion of his analysis of the TSE ruling that condemned former governor Cláudio Castro, citing the decision’s complexity and contradictions. The case has been suspended since April 9, with four justices favoring indirect election and one favoring direct election.

item.title: Minha Casa, Minha Vida se converteu em mera vitrine eleitoral do governo
item.description: The Minha Casa, Minha Vida (MCMV) program has been criticized for becoming a mere electoral showcase for the Lula government, expanding income ceilings and property value limits to target the middle class rather than focusing solely on low-income housing. With a record budget of R$ 200 billion and a goal of 3 million units contracted between 2023 and 2026, the program is seen as a strategy to regain popularity amid declining poll numbers.

item.title: Choque Zema x Gilmar abre campanha
item.description: The 2026 electoral campaign has officially begun, with Lula leveraging Trump’s figure as a strategic asset to bolster his own position and weaken his opponent. The highlight was the debate between Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema and Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, which generated significant exposure for Zema and likely improved his polling numbers despite being considered an underdog. The article emphasizes the boldness of Zema’s team, which produced an animated critique of STF ministers.

item.title: Política externa terá peso na eleição
item.description: Foreign policy, traditionally irrelevant in Brazilian presidential elections, may become decisively important in 2026 due to the direct impact of international choices on citizens' daily lives — such as fuel prices, technological dependence, and supply chain vulnerabilities. The article suggests that, for the first time since redemocratization, foreign policy missteps could be tangibly felt by the population, making it a central campaign issue.

item.title: Descontos de até 90%, juro mais baixo e saque do FGTS: o que já se sabe sobre o novo Desenrola
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan met with bank CEOs to finalize details of the federal government's debt renegotiation program, 'Desenrola', which President Lula is set to announce by May 1st. The program will offer discounts of up to 90% on debts, reduced interest rates of approximately 1.99% per month, and allow the use of FGTS as collateral. The article is exclusive to GLOBO subscribers.

item.title: As sinalizações do Planalto a Hugo Motta sobre a redução da 'taxa das blusinhas'
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta has received signals from the Planalto Palace indicating the government is inclined to send a proposal to Congress to eliminate the so-called 'blusinhas tax' — a 20% levy on imports under US$50. Although internal executive debate remains unresolved, growing electoral pressure is favoring the political faction advocating for the tax's repeal. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Lula assina hoje promulgação do acordo Mercosul–UE e conclui ratificação brasileira do tratado após 27 anos de negociações
item.description: President Lula signed today the promulgation of the Mercosul–EU trade agreement, completing Brazil’s ratification after 27 years of negotiations. The treaty covers approximately 718 million people and a combined GDP exceeding US$22 trillion, providing for gradual tariff reductions on industrial and agricultural goods, as well as rules on investments, services, public procurement, and intellectual property. Government simulations project a 0.34% increase in Brazil’s GDP by 2044 (equivalent to R$37 billion), alongside 0.76% growth in investment and 2.65% growth in Brazilian exports.

item.title: Ciro Nogueira quer apoio de Tarcísio e espera acordo na próxima semana
item.description: Ciro Nogueira, national president of the PP, said he expects support from Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) for a center-right political arrangement in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Minas Gerais, with an announcement expected next Monday. He stated that the federation’s leadership will be decided by the national party leaders and stressed the importance of unity between center and right to prevent fragmentation that would benefit the left in the São Paulo Senate race.

item.title: Palumbo e Rufino serão os nomes do Podemos ao Senado em SP
item.description: The national president of Podemos, Renata Abreu, announced that the party will field two names for the São Paulo Senate race in 2026: federal deputy Delegado Palumbo and businessman Geraldo Rufino, with one to be chosen as the candidate. She also confirmed Podemos’ support for Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, citing frequent dialogue and positive evaluation of his administration, while the party will launch its own Senate candidacy. Nationally, Renata stated that Podemos is currently aligned with center-right, but presidential support will depend on internal consultations and a candidate advocating a moderate and balanced discourse, as the presidential race remains open and competitive.

item.title: Haddad usa fala de Ana Paula Renault para defender fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: Former Finance Minister and São Paulo gubernatorial pre-candidate Fernando Haddad (PT) used statements from BBB 2026 winner Ana Paula Renault to advocate for reducing the workweek from 44 to 40 hours (5X2 model), sharing a video in which she emphasizes historic labor rights victories despite conservative opposition. Haddad mobilized public support to pressure Congress into approving Lula’s urgent labor reform bill, citing opposition from figures such as Valdemar Costa Neto (PL) and Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos).

item.title: Não vejo espaço nenhum para terceira via enquanto Lula e Bolsonaro forem vivos, diz Ciro Nogueira
item.description: PP president Senator Ciro Nogueira (PI) stated there is no room for a third way in the presidential race while Lula (PT) and Jair Bolsonaro (PL) are alive. The comment was made during an event in São Paulo on Monday night.

item.title: PL pede que PGR investigue PT por vídeo associando Flávio Bolsonaro ao Banco Master
item.description: Federal deputy Ubiratan Sanderson (PL-RS) has requested the Attorney General's Office (PGR) to investigate the Workers' Party (PT) over a video that associates Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, with the Banco Master scandal. The request was made on Monday, April 27, following the video's release on Sunday, April 26. The accusation alleges that the PT is attempting to link Bolsonaro to a corruption scheme involving Banco Master.

item.title: “A democracia não existe no Maranhão”, diz Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate for presidency from the Missão party, claimed that Maranhão lives under a political exception regime and that democracy does not exist in the state, labeling the local ruling class as parasitic. He proposes deep structural interventions, including restricting voting rights in municipalities with low development indicators, and advocates a 'law and order' agenda with states of defense in criminal-dominated territories and harsher penalties against 'enemies of the State'. His campaign strategy targets young male voters (up to 24 years old) through a donor-funded road caravan to increase awareness of his platform.

item.title: “Não entrei na vida pública para enriquecer, ao contrário de certas pessoas”, diz Zema a Dirceu
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) rebutted accusations from former minister José Dirceu (PT) that he had increased his own salary during his term, stating he donated his entire gubernatorial salary. Zema emphasized that he did not enter public life to enrich himself, contrasting his conduct with that of certain politicians.

item.title: Eleição está nas mãos de Flávio, diz Ciro Nogueira
item.description: Ciro Nogueira, president of the PP, stated that the outcome of the 2026 presidential election depends on the decisions of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), calling the current scenario undefined. He noted that the decisive electorate represents about 13% of voters, concentrated in Minas Gerais and São Paulo, and advocated for a candidate who can reduce polarization and unite Brazil.

item.title: Não tem espaço para a 3ª via, diz Ciro Nogueira sobre as eleições
item.description: Ciro Nogueira, president of the PP, states there is no space for a third-way candidacy in the 2026 elections while Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Jair Bolsonaro remain central references in Brazilian politics. He says the race remains undefined and will be decided by around 13% of the electorate, concentrated in Minas Gerais and São Paulo — moderate and conservative voters seeking to reduce polarization and prioritize a future-oriented agenda.

item.title: Ciro Nogueira diz que eleição será decidida na ‘margem de erro’ e não vê espaço para terceira via
item.description: Ciro Nogueira, president of the PP, states that the 2026 presidential election will be decided by the 'margin of error' and that there is no room for a third way while Lula and Bolsonaro remain alive, as voters are driven by rejection. He suggests Flávio Bolsonaro could win if he focuses on unifying the country and avoids past debates like January 8, and that the Banco Master scandal will not be decisive. He notes that around 13% of undecided voters, concentrated in Minas Gerais and São Paulo, will determine the outcome.

item.title: PF manda empresário tirar faixa que dizia “ladrão” próximo a evento que Lula participaria
item.description: The Federal Police ordered a businessman in Presidente Prudente, SP, to remove a banner reading 'thief' aimed at President Lula, after he had planned to attend an event in the city. Although Lula’s visit was canceled due to scheduling, the businessman had put up the banner the previous week, prompting police action. The incident was reported by O Antagonista.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia propõe criar 'brigadas eleitorais' para candidatas mulheres nas eleições 2026
item.description: Supreme Federal Court Justice Cármen Lúcia proposed the creation of 'electoral brigades' to ensure the safety of female candidates in the 2026 elections. The proposal was made during a lecture at UFRGS on contemporary challenges and pathways to combat violence against women.
